content.user_title: Secure Payment Systems for PCI DSS
content.value_statement: Payment systems create compliance risk when cardholder data is stored or transmitted incorrectly. This skill gives practical PCI DSS guidance for safer payment design and assessment readiness.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes the 12 core PCI DSS requirement areas.
Explains which payment data must never be stored.
Shows tokenization patterns for processor-based payment flows.
Outlines encryption at rest and TLS controls for cardholder data.
Provides access control, audit logging, and monitoring guidance.
Compares SAQ A, SAQ A-EP, and SAQ D scenarios.
limitations: Does not replace official PCI DSS standards or QSA advice.
Does not run automated compliance scans or evidence collection.
Code examples are illustrative and need production review.
Provider-specific requirements may require separate documentation.

use_cases.title: Design a tokenized checkout flow
use_cases.description: Plan a payment flow that keeps raw card data away from application servers.

use_cases.title: Prepare PCI DSS control evidence
use_cases.description: Map system controls to PCI DSS areas before an internal review or assessment.

use_cases.title: Reduce payment compliance scope
use_cases.description: Identify hosted payment, tokenization, and segmentation choices that reduce cardholder data exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Identify PCI Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my payment flow and identify which systems store, process, or transmit cardholder data. Recommend ways to reduce PCI scope.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tokenized Payments
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a tokenized payment flow using a hosted processor. Include what data my server should and should not receive.

prompt_templates.title: Review Storage Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess my planned storage model for PAN, tokens, customer identifiers, logs, and audit records. Flag PCI DSS data protection gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Assessment Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PCI DSS evidence checklist for my cardholder data environment, including access control, encryption, logging, testing, and policy artifacts.

output_examples.input: Review a checkout architecture that sends card numbers to the application server.
output_examples.output: The response would identify direct cardholder data handling, recommend hosted fields or checkout, and list systems that remain in PCI scope.

output_examples.input: Plan storage for payment methods and customer billing records.
output_examples.output: The response would separate prohibited data from allowed identifiers, recommend token storage, and describe encryption and access controls.

output_examples.input: Prepare for a PCI DSS self-assessment.
output_examples.output: The response would outline likely SAQ fit, evidence to collect, control owners, and gaps to review before formal assessment.

best_practices: Use hosted payment pages or processor tokens when possible.
Treat all examples as design guidance, not production-ready code.
Validate recommendations against current PCI DSS requirements and assessor guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not store CVV, track data, PINs, or unmasked card numbers.
Do not copy placeholder API keys or encryption examples into production.
Do not assume tokenization removes every PCI DSS obligation.

faq.question: Does this skill make a system PCI compliant?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, but compliance requires validated controls, evidence, and applicable assessment steps.

faq.question: Can it replace a Qualified Security Assessor?
faq.answer: No. Use it for preparation and design support, then confirm requirements with a QSA or official PCI guidance.

faq.question: Does it support hosted checkout designs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains hosted payments, tokenization, and data minimization patterns that reduce cardholder data exposure.

faq.question: Does it include code examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes illustrative examples for tokenization, encryption, access control, audit logging, and validation.

faq.question: Can it help choose a PCI SAQ type?
faq.answer: It can explain common SAQ A, SAQ A-EP, and SAQ D differences, but final selection depends on your environment.

faq.question: Is this useful with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance can support architecture reviews, implementation planning, and compliance preparation in those tools.
